# Temple Scroll Column 67 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 67 | **Condition:** fragmentary (final column)

---

**67:1** You will be blessed in the city and blessed in the countryside.

**67:2** Your children will be blessed, your crops will be blessed, and your livestock will be blessed — your calves and your lambs alike.

**67:3** Your bread basket and your mixing bowl will be blessed.

**67:4** You will be blessed wherever you go — coming in and going out.

**67:5** The LORD will defeat the enemies who attack you. They will come at you from one direction but scatter in seven directions, running for their lives.

**67:6** But if you refuse to obey the LORD your God and fail to follow all his commands and decrees, [...] all these curses will come crashing down on you.

**67:7** You will be cursed in the city and cursed in the countryside.

**67:8** Your bread basket and your mixing bowl will be cursed.

**67:9** Your children will be cursed, your crops will be cursed, your calves and your lambs will be cursed. [...]

**67:10** [...] The LORD will strike you with disaster, confusion, and defeat in everything you try to do, until you are ruined and quickly destroyed — all because you abandoned me and chose evil.

**67:11** [...] The LORD will plague you with disease until you are wiped out from the land you are entering to possess. [...]

**67:12** [...] All this because you refused to serve the LORD your God with joy and happiness when you had everything in abundance. [...]

**67:13** [...] Instead you will serve the enemies the LORD sends against you — starving, thirsty, naked, and lacking everything. He will put an iron yoke on your neck until you are destroyed. [...]

**67:14** [...] All these curses will hunt you down until you are destroyed, because you refused to obey the LORD your God and follow his commands and decrees. [...]

---

*PNEUMA notes: The Temple Scroll ends in ruins — both literally and thematically. Column 67 moves from radiant blessings to devastating curses, and the manuscript itself breaks apart as the curses intensify. The symmetry is haunting: every blessing has its mirror curse. "Because you abandoned me" — even at the bitter end, God speaks in first person, making the covenant rupture achingly personal. The iron yoke image (67:13) finds its echo in Jeremiah 28. The scroll's ending is lost to time, leaving the curses hanging in the air, unresolved.*
